metaDescription: Three genuine 90 pint dehumidifiers compared on drain options, pump lift, tank size and app control, with honest advice on rated versus real output.
expertTake: The avylo with its built-in 15 foot pump is the best 90 pint unit for a basement whose drain is out of reach. The ARLIME is the plain, roomy choice for a floor-drain setup. If you need only the standard 50 or 60 pint class, do not pay for a 90 pint cabinet.
introParagraphs: Capacity labels in this class are crowded with numbers that do not mean the same thing. Some listings use a lab figure measured in a hot, saturated test room, some quote an older scale and some bundle a coverage claim that assumes a lightly damp space.

Real genuine 90 pint machines are rarer than the keyword suggests, because many listings blend in larger commercial units or smaller home models. Sorting them comes down to the size of the problem you have, the drain you can reach and the controls you will actually use.

products.name: avylo 90 Pint Dehumidifier With Built-In Pump, 5,000 sq ft
products.description:
avylo makes the most complete 90 pint package in this group: a built-in pump with a 15 foot reach, a 2.11 gallon top-mounted tank with automatic shutoff, and a Most Efficient 2025 rating at 2.05 liters per kilowatt hour. That combination means three ways to drain and a lower electric bill than a standard cabinet at the same capacity.

A pump is the feature that most separates this model from its rivals. Where the ARLIME and Pauvoern depend on gravity or a bucket, the avylo can push water up and out of a basement, which opens up laundry standpipes and sink drains that a gravity unit could never reach. The top-mounted tank also keeps the lift of a full bucket at waist height instead of off the floor.

The same machine appears in both black and white listings under slightly different titles, so treat them as one model. Plan for the usual pump upkeep: run clean water through it each spring and make sure the tube slopes without dips. It lands near the middle of the price tiers for this size, which is good value for a machine carrying a pump and the efficiency badge. Noise is the area where a pump unit can disappoint: besides the compressor hum, you will hear a short whir each time the internal reservoir empties, so place it in a utility corner rather than beside a sleeping area. Its coverage claim of 5,000 sq ft is smaller than the ARLIME's 6,000, but that figure rests on mild assumptions anyway, and the drain flexibility matters more in daily use.

products.name: ARLIME 90 Pint Dehumidifier, 6,000 sq ft, 2.2 gal tank

specList.label: Headline rating
specList.value: Up to 90 pints per day at 95F and 90% RH

products.description:
ARLIME states its test condition plainly, 95F and 90% RH, which makes the 90 pint figure easier to interpret than a bare number. The coverage claim of 6,000 sq ft is the largest in the group, and the 8.4 liter tank is the biggest bucket here, so it works for a large open basement or a ground-floor space where you want to empty it less often.

The listing mentions three drain methods but no built-in pump, so the realistic setups are the bucket and a gravity hose. That suits a house with a floor drain right beside the machine and rules out a laundry sink across the room. A high-density outer filter doubles as a dust screen, which helps in a workshop but needs frequent cleaning because it clogs faster than a coarse mesh.

In the price tiers it sits low, well below the avylo. The tradeoff is clear: you give up the pump and the Most Efficient badge in exchange for a large tank and a simpler machine. Keep the cabinet 6 to 12 inches from walls, and wash the outer filter every couple of weeks during the humid months. Because the machine lacks a pump, think about where the hose leaves the cabinet and keep it sloping down the whole way, since a hose with a rise in the middle will trap water and trip the shutoff. An 8.4 liter bucket also makes a decent backup when a hose pops off a fitting while you are away.

products.name: Pauvoern 90 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier With Wi-Fi
products.description:
Pauvoern is the connected option. A touchscreen on the cabinet and the Tuya Smart app give you control of four operating modes and a three-speed fan from a phone, which is useful when the machine lives in a basement you visit rarely. It carries a 2024 Energy Star certification rather than the newer Most Efficient 2025 mark.

The tank is the smallest of the three at 1.45 gallons, which means a 90 pint machine in a wet space will fill it quickly. Use the drain hose for anything beyond occasional use. With no pump on the listing, the drain has to be at or below the machine's outlet, and the app is no help if your Wi-Fi does not reach the basement.

In the price tiers this is the cheapest of the three, which makes sense because the connected features come at low cost on the Tuya platform. Check that the cabinet's local humidistat still works without the cloud, since a phone-only setpoint is a risk when the router fails. For many buyers the best arrangement is the avylo for hard drains and the Pauvoern for a simple, monitored room. The four-mode layout is helpful in practice: a continuous mode for peak summer, a timed or auto mode for shoulder seasons, and a fan-only mode to dry a damp floor after cleaning. Compared with the ARLIME, you give up a roughly one gallon smaller bucket and gain app logging of humidity, which is a fair swap for a hose-drained machine.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Many listings returned for this size are 80, 95, 105 or 120 pint machines, or small Peltier cabinets with a bucket measured in ounces. A real compressor unit in this class weighs over 40 pounds and draws more than 500 watts. The avylo, ARLIME and Pauvoern all state 90 pints in the listing, which is why they appear here. Always confirm the number and its test condition before trusting a headline.

ARLIME quotes 90 pints at 95F and 90% RH. Under the DOE test used since 2019, at 65F and 60% RH, the same capacity reads about 40 percent lower, which is why a modern 90 pint label can correspond to roughly 50 to 55 pints in a cool basement. Size the machine to your space, and consider the 90 pint rating a ceiling, not a promise. A practical test is to run the machine for 24 hours with a separate meter in the room and see how long it takes to bring the reading from the wet starting point down to 50 percent.

A pump is worth the added complexity only when your drain is higher than the machine or more than a few feet away. The avylo pumps water up to 15 feet. The ARLIME and Pauvoern need a gravity path, so a floor drain within a hose length is a requirement for them. Without one, you are back to emptying the bucket.

At a rating of this size a damp room can fill a one-gallon tank in under a day. The ARLIME holds 2.2 gallons, the avylo 2.11 and the Pauvoern 1.45. A full-tank shutoff protects your floor but also stops the dehumidifier, so a hose is almost always the better arrangement for a machine that is meant to run unattended. If you must use the bucket, empty it before bed so the unit does not stop in the middle of the night with the room still damp.

Electricity is the largest ownership cost for a compressor machine that cycles all summer. The avylo carries Most Efficient 2025 at 2.05 liters per kilowatt hour, and the Pauvoern lists a 2024 Energy Star mark. If you will run the unit more than 8 hours daily, the efficiency tier can offset a higher purchase price within a couple of seasons.

All compressor machines lose capacity as the air cools, and below about 65F the coil frosts. Auto defrost helps, but a 90 pint machine in a 55F basement may deliver half its label. If your space routinely runs that cool, a low-temperature unit is the better tool, and no model in this lineup is built for it.

specDecoder.meaning: The same compressor produces different numbers depending on the air it is fed. A hot, saturated test gives the highest figure and a cooler test gives the lowest.
specDecoder.watchFor: ARLIME states 95F and 90% RH, while the others leave the condition to the fine print.

specDecoder.meaning: It is derived from capacity under mild dampness, not from a measured basement. A wet space or a high ceiling can double the effective volume.
specDecoder.watchFor: ARLIME claims 6,000 sq ft, the avylo 5,000 and the Pauvoern 5,500, but the gaps do not reflect different machines.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the vertical distance a condensate pump can push water. The usable figure falls as the discharge tube gets longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the avylo has a pump, rated at 15 feet.

specDecoder.meaning: The efficiency metric behind Energy Star, showing how much water is removed per unit of electricity. A higher number means a lower running cost.
specDecoder.watchFor: Avylo lists 2.05 L/kWh; check whether others publish a figure.

specDecoder.meaning: The bucket sets how long the machine runs before the float shuts it off. A larger tank means fewer interruptions but a heavier lift.
specDecoder.watchFor: The ARLIME's 8.4 L tank weighs about 18 pounds when full.

howWeEvaluated.title: Genuine 90 pint filter
howWeEvaluated.description: We discarded listings that were 80 pint, 105 pint, 150 pint, 190 pint or small Peltier units and kept only machines that name 90 pints. That left three real choices, so none of them is padded with an off-size stand-in.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drain flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: Each unit was judged on how many ways it can drain and whether it can move water without gravity. The avylo's 15 foot pump is the standout, and tank sizes of 2.2, 2.11 and 1.45 gallons were weighed as a fallback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency evidence
howWeEvaluated.description: Reading each spec sheet closely, we favored units that quote an efficiency number, such as the avylo's 2.05 L/kWh. Plain Energy Star claims were counted but weighted below a measurable efficiency figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control quality
howWeEvaluated.description: App connectivity, display clarity and humidistat behavior were compared. Pauvoern's touchscreen and Tuya app give the most remote control, while the others lean on a conventional panel.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: Complaints and praise that recur were weighed: filter clogging, pump noise, bucket slime and compressor longevity. Compressors in this class typically last 5 to 10 years, and low-priced units cluster at the shorter end.

cards.label: With a pump
cards.text: The avylo can lift condensate to a sink or standpipe 15 feet up, so the machine can sit wherever it works best, not wherever the floor drain is. You trade simplicity for flexibility, and you must run clean water through the pump periodically.

cards.label: Without a pump
cards.text: The ARLIME and Pauvoern rely on gravity or a bucket. They have fewer failure points and cost less, but the drain must sit at or below the machine's outlet. If your drain is far from the machine, the hose will need to run along the floor.

howToChoose.note: Pick the pump only if gravity cannot reach your drain. If you can run a hose along the floor to a drain at or below the machine's outlet, the ARLIME or Pauvoern will do the same job with fewer moving parts and a lower price tier.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A continuous drain, a high pump or hose reach and a tank big enough to survive a full day. Size up if the walls feel damp, and add a hygrometer so you can see whether the machine is reaching 45 to 50 percent.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The avylo handles the widest range of drains, and the ARLIME has the largest tank. Between them, pick the avylo when the drain is awkward and the ARLIME when a floor drain sits next to the machine.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You will run the unit most of the summer and need unattended drainage. The avylo's pump and Most Efficient rating pay off in labor and electricity, and it will work in rooms where a gravity hose cannot.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The room has a floor drain and the humidity problem is seasonal. The ARLIME or Pauvoern provides 90 pints of rated capacity at lower price tiers, and the savings buy a hygrometer and a spare filter.

maintenance.why: A loaded filter reduces airflow and forces the compressor to work harder. Rinse it, dry it and refit it before restarting.
Slime on the float switch causes false full-tank shutoffs. A quick rinse with mild soap keeps the reading honest.

maintenance.task: Run the pump with fresh water
maintenance.why: A pump that sits dry for months can stick. Pour clean water into the tank and confirm it discharges through the tube.
Lint and dust cut heat transfer and lengthen run times. Unplug the unit and use a soft brush.

maintenance.task: Compare the display with a hygrometer
maintenance.why: Sensors drift and a 5 percent error is common. A cheap reference meter tells you whether to nudge the setpoint.

faq.q: Is 90 pints too much for a typical basement?
faq.a: Not for a damp one. Because the label is a hot-room figure, a cool basement yields a much smaller real number, and a machine with spare capacity cycles off sooner. For a lightly humid room under 1,500 sq ft, a smaller unit is cheaper.

faq.q: Why are there so few true 90 pint models?
faq.a: The market clusters around 50, 70, 80 and 95 pints. Many listings that mention 90 are older ratings or approximations, so we kept only units that name the figure and are real compressor machines.

faq.q: Do I need the pump version?
faq.a: Only if gravity cannot reach a drain. The avylo is the single pump unit here. If a floor drain sits near the machine, the ARLIME gives you a bigger tank at a lower price.

faq.q: How much electricity will it use?
faq.a: A compressor machine at this size draws roughly 500 to 800 watts while running. The avylo's Most Efficient rating at 2.05 L/kWh moves less of that into your bill than a standard unit, but actual cost depends on hours of operation.

faq.q: Will it work in a cold basement?
faq.a: It will run, but capacity drops as the coil cools and auto defrost cycles interrupt drying. Below about 60F, a low-temperature commercial unit is a better match. A vapor barrier over a dirt floor or sealing a leaking foundation crack usually does more for the problem than a bigger machine.

faq.q: Is the app worth caring about?
faq.a: It is a convenience, not a necessity. The Pauvoern's app is helpful for a remote room, but make sure the panel still controls the unit during a network outage.
